title: Quarterly dedicated pool autoscale playbook: ramp, surge & SLA harmonization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Overview: Create an executable quarterly playbook that aligns dedicated GPU pool ramping, surge handling, and autoscale policies with SLOs and customer commitments. The playbook will standardize (1) pre-warm / ramp heuristics, (2) surge reservoir usage, (3) fallback model routing, and (4) incident and rollback procedures for Dedicated customers. Background: Q4 experiments showed high cost during sudden enterprise bursts and unclear guardrails for routing to hosted fallbacks. This ticket consolidates learnings into a single operational artifact and ties the playbook to measurable OKRs (P95 latency, failover success rate, and cost delta per 1M tokens).

Scope/In-scope: - Policy definitions for ramp windows (pre-warm thresholds, warmup durations) - Surge reservoir sizing guidance per pool tier - Autoscale governor settings and priority sharding rules - Runbooks for canary-to-global rollouts and immediate fallback triggers - Dashboard metrics to surface during ramp/surge (heatmap, reservoir utilization, throttles)

Out of scope: per-customer bespoke contracts, on-prem packaging (tracked in PM-71512).

Proposed approach: 1) Define baseline heuristics using historical traffic (last 90 days) and simulation tool (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-lab PR #412). 2) Produce parametric templates for small/medium/large pools. 3) Implement new dashboard slices in Grafana (dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/AB12/autoscale-runbook) for visibility. 4) Draft canary checklist and post-mortem template.

Acceptance criteria: - Playbook doc (Confluence) published and reviewed by ENG, SRE, and Sales (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/QA+Autoscale+Playbook) - Runbook templates for canary and global rollout exist and are validated in staging with recorded dry-run (video link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c) - Dashboard surfaces reservoir metrics and P95 latency within the first 2 minutes of a simulated surge - One cross-functional rehearsal completed with incident drill and summary created - OKR: reduce median surge cost-per-token by at least 7% in controlled experiment compared to baseline

Metrics and monitoring: Primary metrics: P95 latency, failover success rate, reservoir utilization, cost delta per 1M tokens. Secondary: throttles/sec, queue depth, KV cache hit rate during ramp.

Stakeholders: Product: Maya Chen (owner), Eng: Priya Rangan (runtime), SRE: Omar Blake, Sales/CS: Fiona Duan. Approval required from Head of Product and SRE lead.

Risks & mitigation: - Oversized reservoirs increase cost: mitigation -> run simulation and cap spend via policy flags. - Unexpected routing loops in fallback logic: mitigation -> static rollout with feature flag and extra tracing.

Deliverables: - Confluence playbook + parametric templates - Grafana dashboard slices + alert rules - Canary checklist + rehearsal write-up - PRs that add simulation tests and toggle flags (see github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-lab PR #412 and PR #427) - Hand-off runbook to Capacity Ops and Customer Success

Next steps: 1) Align metrics with SRE and set baseline (owner: Priya) by 2026-01-20. 2) Complete simulation runs for three representative enterprise customers by 2026-01-30. 3) Draft playbook for review by 2026-02-05. 4) Schedule rehearsal in cycle 2026-W07.
